messages.subject: baf vs. mufreq & avg.depth.ratio
messages.body_plain:
Hi -- thanks for making this tool.  I had two questions.

First, when is it better to use the mufreq method instead of baf?  The documentation says that mufreq is more noisy -- how much more data does it need?  If there is a lot of data, is mufreq more accurate?

Second, I see in workflows.R that there are four different ways to calculate avg.depth.ratio:

      #avg.depth.ratio <- mean(sequenza.extract$gc$adj[,2])
      #avg.depth.ratio <- weighted.mean(x = segs.all$depth.ratio, w = segs.len)
      #avg.depth.ratio <- center.ratio(segs.all)
      avg.depth.ratio <- 1

Which is advisable?  I tried using mean(sequenza.extract$gc$adj[,2]), but it always evaluates to 1.

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: baf vs. mufreq & avg.depth.ratio
messages.body_plain:
Hi George,

Tanks for trying sequenza!

I recommend using the baf method for whole gnoeme/exome sequencing. You can try the mufreq method with validation cohort, but we didn’t test it that much.

The “mufreq” method works nicely when you have validation sequencing, eg: ionTorrent or miSeq.
So you need more data, meaning more deep sequencing. That way you would have the mutation frequency calculated using ~1000 of reads instead of 20/150 reads usually available by WGS or exome seq.

The mufreq method could eventually work if you remove the low-frequency-mutations - derived by sequencing error/misalignments - But by doing that, you introduce a bias (you are basically selecting the frequency you want…). Alternatively, if you have a robust way to filter and/or validate the mutations, you can run the mufreq method only on the subset of robust-called mutations

About the avg.depth.ratio in the code, I originally used mean(sequenza.extract$gc$adj[,2]), then some user was reporting weird estimations, depending on the specific bias present in the data: the normalisation was able to adjust the average depth ratio, but the segments average was much lower then 1.
Long story short, I’ve tried different solutions (the various commented lines) then I resolved that the average depth ratio, after normalisation as we perform it, should be 1. As you notices mean(sequenza.extract$gc$adj[,2]) is always 1, so there was no point of using that way to calculate it, instead I just hardcoded the value.

Of course if you are developing alternative workflow you can try different alternative: in theory, using the model you can read in the manuscript, it should be equal to the average depth in the tumor divided by average depth in the normal sequencing.

I hope my comment were useful
Don’t hesitate of make other questions.

Francesco
